blocks.heading: Chanukah, the Yom Tov of Aharon and the kohanim

paragraphs.text: The Mashgiach opens with Rashi's explanation that Aharon was pained at having no part in the inauguration of the nesi'im and was given the lights, which the Ramban says means the Chanukah lights. The nesi'im had their Yom Tov in the twelve days of Nissan; Chanukah is the Yom Tov of Aharon and the kohanim.

Through the Chanukah lights Aharon inaugurates every Jewish home as a Beis Hamikdash. From Rabbeinu Bechaye, which the Bnei Yissaschar also brings, the Mashgiach adds that the eight lights correspond to the names of Moshiach.

blocks.heading: The seudah that strengthens emunah in Moshiach

paragraphs.text: The seudah of Zos Chanukah, the Mashgiach explains, is there to strengthen the emunah in Moshiach, since what a person eats becomes part of his life. He brings the Smag, who counts hoping for the yeshuah within the mitzvah of Anochi: Hashem who took us out of Mitzrayim will redeem again. Lighting Chanukah candles kindles the light of Moshiach in every home, the 'lamp for My anointed'.

blocks.heading: Hod, Hallel and the years of Aharon

paragraphs.text: Aharon is the middah of hod, and the sefarim say that Chanukah is in hod; therefore Chanukah is the day of thanks and Hallel. The Mashgiach notes that the Rambam places all the laws of Hallel within the laws of Chanukah, because Chanukah is the root of Hallel, and connects the Hallelukahs to Aharon's years.

He then asks why Parshas Masei gives Aharon's age and his passing on Rosh Chodesh Av, details not given where his death is told. He answers that Masei speaks of the exiles, and there Aharon stands not as a person but for the Beis Hamikdash; his passing hints to its destruction.

When Jews light the menorah they build the Beis Hamikdash: each generation adds a piece to the menorah in Heaven, which will come down when it is complete. The great early generations made its upper parts, the cups and flowers; the later ones make its lower part. Parshas Beha'aloscha, following the Ramban, speaks of this menorah, made through lighting Chanukah candles.

The Chanukah haftorah promises 'My servant Tzemach': like a sprout growing unseen beneath the ground, lighting the candles brings Moshiach. The verse says 'raising' and not 'kindling' because it speaks of the Chanukah menorah, where a new light is added each day.

Our low generations make the base of the menorah. Yet, as the Tanya says in chapter two, the lowest souls are bound to the highest, and the menorah is 'one hammered piece from its base to its flowers'.

blocks.heading: Zos Chanukah, the day of the seal

paragraphs.text: The Mashgiach speaks of a world called Klal Yisrael, which he brings from the Noam Elimelech, where all souls are fused together and equal, the lowest bound to the greatest. This, he explains, is the praise of Aharon that he did not change: the menorah he lit is one piece joining all Jews to their root, where there is no change.

Zos Chanukah is the day of the chasimah. As Unesaneh Tokef says, each person's own hand signs, so each Jew makes his seal through his avodah: preparing the menorah, lighting, Hallel and Al Hanisim. The Mashgiach adds that there is still time to ask Hashem, bind oneself to the Kohen Gadol and make a good chasimah for all Klal Yisrael, and closes with a tefilah for the complete redemption.
